q: In the National Building Code's definitions, what term is used for a physical change made to a building that adds to its value, usefulness, or appearance?
n: “RENOVATION — Any physical change made on buildings/structures to increase the value, quality, and/or to improve the aesthetic.” This is distinct from Repair, which restores a damaged portion to its original condition.

q: What is the maximum total cost allowed for a dwelling to qualify as a traditional indigenous family dwelling under the National Building Code?
n: A “traditional indigenous family dwelling” is defined as one built of native materials (bamboo, nipa, logs, or lumber) for the owner's family only, “the total cost of which does not exceed fifteen thousand pesos (₱15,000.00).”

q: A building permit is required before undertaking which of the following?
o: Repair of a load-bearing partition wall
An open terrace measuring 15 square meters
A garden pool with a depth of 500 millimeters or less
Repair of a door, floor, window, or fence
ref: IRR Rule III, §301 — Work Exempt from Building Permit
n: Section 301 exempts only “repair and/or replacement of non load-bearing partition walls,” along with repairs of doors, windows, flooring, and fences. Load-bearing (structural) repairs are never on that exempt list, so they still need a permit.

q: Within his territorial jurisdiction, who is responsible for enforcing the National Building Code and holds the authority to issue, deny, suspend, or revoke building permits?
ref: PD 1096, §207 — Duties of a Building Official
n: “In his respective territorial jurisdiction, the Building Official shall be primarily responsible for the enforcement of the provisions of this Code... He is the official charged with the duties of issuing building permits.”

q: Which of the following is exempt from payment of building permit fees?
o: Buildings owned by the government for public use
A single-family home built of native materials costing not more than PHP15,000
n: “Public buildings and traditional indigenous family dwelling[s] shall be exempt from payment of building permit fees.” The dwelling-cost option restates that same traditional-dwelling exemption, capped at ₱15,000.

q: At least how many sets of plans and specifications must be submitted with a building permit application?
ref: PD 1096 / IRR Rule III, §302(3) — Application for Permits
n: “To be submitted together with such application are at least five (5) sets of corresponding plans and specifications prepared, signed and sealed by...” the relevant licensed professionals.

q: Per Article 1723 of the Civil Code, who is held liable when a building collapses because of a defect in the plans?
o: The engineer or architect who prepared the design
The building contractor together with the site construction supervisor
The Building Official who reviewed and approved said plans
ref: Civil Code of the Philippines, Art. 1723
n: The contractor is not liable because the cause of the collapse isn't defective construction or inferior materials, and the Building Official is never implicated in Article 1723.

q: Which certificate must be secured before a completed building may be used or occupied?
n: “No building or structure shall be used or occupied... until the Building Official has issued a Certificate of Occupancy therefor.”

q: What professional qualification must the full-time construction inspector engaged by the owner possess?
ref: PD 1096, §308 — Inspection and Supervision of Work
n: “The owner of the Building... shall engage the services of a duly licensed architect or civil engineer to undertake the full time inspection and supervision of the construction work.”

q: What term describes new construction that increases the height or floor area of an existing building?
n: “ADDITION — Any new construction which increases the height and/or floor area of an existing building/structure.”

q: Which construction type is rated four-hour fire-resistive throughout its structural elements?
ref: PD 1096 / IRR Rule IV, §401 — Types of Construction
n: “Type V — [Construction] shall be four-hour fire-resistive throughout and the structural elements shall be of steel, iron, concrete, or masonry construction,” the only type rated four-hour all through.

q: The National Building Code applies to all public and private buildings except those covered by which of the following?
o: Projects involving only alteration and renovation
ref: IRR Rule I, §103 — Scope and Application
n: Section 103 applies the Code to all buildings/structures “except traditional indigenous family dwellings... and those covered by Batas Pambansa Bilang 220,” i.e. Economic and Socialized Housing Projects. Traditional family dwellings aren't in the choices, leaving BP 220 as the answer.

q: In which fire zone is Type III construction permitted?
ref: IRR of PD 1096, Rule V, Sec. 5.1 — Fire Zones
n: The IRR allows Types II to IV in fire restrictive zones; non-fire-restricted zones take only Types I and II, and highly fire restrictive zones only Types IV and V.

q: Which type of repair work requires a building permit?
o: Replacing all drywall partitions in a three-story residence
Repairing a load-bearing beam that supports a secondary balcony
Fixing a solid wood door used as an exit
None of these require a permit
ref: IRR Rule III, §301 — Work Exempt from Building Permit
n: Section 301's exemption list covers only non-load-bearing items — doors, windows, flooring, fences, non-bearing partitions. A structural beam, even a minor one, is a load-bearing element and isn't on that list.

q: Which of the following is NOT among the grounds for declaring a building dangerous or ruinous?
ref: PD 1096 / IRR Rule II, §214 — Dangerous and Ruinous Buildings or Structures
n: Section 214's grounds include structural hazard, fire hazard, and hazardous electrical/mechanical installations, plus “architectural deficiency” — not “aesthetic deficiency,” which is the wrong term.
